@graph.evidence: The 2008 benchmark expressly requires relating Earth-system and astronomical conditions to global climate change. The 2026 climate sequence specifies regulation mechanisms; no located climate-cluster benchmark repeats that precise external-forcing relation. Related solar-activity content appears elsewhere. Treat as a candidate partial omission/reframing, not a confirmed deletion.

The 2008 ocean heat/carbon/water influence benchmark has related material in the 2026 ocean-circulation and climate-regulation sequence. A direct benchmark-level link for carbon storage and climate change is less explicit in the cited current sequence.
@graph.status: related concept; explicitness change requires further review

@graph.evidence: Both texts address human activities and Earth-system consequences, but the 1996 statement is specifically about fossil-fuel combustion releasing carbon dioxide, while the 2026 sequence broadly examines anthropogenic system interactions. This is concept-level continuity, not textual borrowing.

The explicit middle-school natural-selection sequence appears at grade 7 in the 2008 standards and grade 8 in the 2026 draft. Core selection concepts remain. This is a grade-placement comparison, not source attribution.
